title: Grateful Dead Live at RFK Stadium on 1973-06-10

ai_review.summary: Audience tape captures a magical three‑set afternoon with an unforgettable Morning Dew opener; the recording is clear enough to enjoy despite slight loss of tightness.
ai_review.review: The concert is remembered as one of the Dead's finest, opening with a killer “Morning Dew” and sustaining bliss across three marathon sets that even featured a jam with the Allman Brothers. Although it’s an audience (AUD) recording rather than a soundboard, the tape delivers strong bass presence and overall clarity, making the performance still highly enjoyable.

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviewers gave five‑star ratings, praising the show’s energy and memorable moments while noting only minor recording limitations typical of audience tapes.

recording_quality.technical_notes: AUD tape with clear overall mix; Phil's bass unusually prominent (likely close to monitor); some loss of the band's tightness compared to board recordings, but no major drop‑outs or distortion reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Three extended sets played back‑to‑back in hot sun; opener set a high bar and the energy carried through the afternoon into an encore jam, creating a seamless, blissful flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned jamming on the encore with the Allman Brothers, indicating strong presence.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass comes through really strongly, possibly due to taper proximity to his monitor.
